## Overview and Didactic Goal

Every other exercise assumes that you know which account you work with, what this account can do and which material you may upload. This exercise settles that **once**. The other exercises only refer to this page.

You work on no source here and write no prompt. You set up your workspace.

## What You Need

- An account with at least one AI system.
- A text file or a word-processor document for your AI log.

**Language**

The guide is in English. The legal texts (GDPR, AI Act) exist in all three course languages. The text of the law is binding.

## Step 1: Settle Account and Tools

Read the following section and answer the five points for your account.

{{< include ../_ai-requirements-full.qmd >}}

### Seminar Paper: Professional or Private Use?

The law calls you a "deployer" as soon as you use an AI system professionally, and it exempts purely private use. A seminar paper lies in between.

**Orientation, not legal advice:** A seminar paper belongs to your studies, not to your private life. Assume for safety that you count as a deployer, unless your university rules otherwise. In daily practice this changes little, because the duties under Article 50(4) apply only on **publication**:

- A seminar paper that only your lecturer reads does not trigger the disclosure duty. The **academic disclosure** still applies (see [Citing](citing.qmd)).
- A published blog post, a podcast or a social-media post on a public question does fall under the duty, unless a person has checked the text and bears editorial responsibility (see [Public History](public-history.qmd)).

## Step 2: Create the AI Log

{{< include ../_ai-log.qmd >}}

Create your log file now, for example `ai-log.md`, and write `## Working environment` as the first heading.

## Step 3: Record Your Working Environment

Under `## Working environment`, enter your answers to the five points from step 1. Use this template:

```markdown
## Working environment

- Tool and version: [name, version]
- Provider: [name]
- Account: [institutional / private], [free / paid]
- Web search: [on / off]
- Read files: [yes / no]
- Reasoning mode: [on / off / not available]
- Memory and chat history: [on / off]
- My university's rules on AI and data protection: [link or "not found, asked on …"]
- Default answer language of the AI: [language]
```

You enter this **once**. If an item changes (for example you switch tools), note the change with its date in the same section.

::: callout-tip

## Check yourself

Answer without looking anything up:

1. Which material do you not upload?
2. Why is "freely accessible" not enough as permission?
3. When must you label AI-generated text as such, and when not?
   :::

## Learning Objectives

After the exercise you can:

- classify the account, cost and tools of your AI system,
- judge which material you must not upload,
- distinguish legal disclosure from academic disclosure,
- create your AI log and record your working environment.
